protect.name: Leaf miner
protect.signs: Young larvae mine into the leaves: short brownish blotches; grown larvae web the leaflets together; badly hit leaflets roll, dry up and look burnt.

prevent.text: Set up a light trap between 8 and 11 pm at ground level.

ref.where: Lambda-cyhalothrin 5 % EC: groundnut, thrips, leafhopper, leaf miner

protect.name: Tobacco caterpillar (Spodoptera)
protect.signs: Freshly hatched larvae scrape the leaves; grown larvae eat whole leaves, leaving only the stalks, as if cattle had grazed the field.
protect.threshold: 8 egg masses per 100 m of row

prevent.text: Grow castor along the border or as an intercrop as a trap crop; collect and destroy egg masses and young larvae.

organic.text: Spray nuclear polyhedrosis virus 1.5 x 10^12 POB/ha with 2.5 kg crude sugar and 250 ml Teepol per ha.

ref.where: Thiamethoxam 12.6 % + Lambda-cyhalothrin 9.5 % ZC: groundnut, leaf eating caterpillar

protect.name: Rust
protect.signs: Orange-brown pustules, first on the underside of the leaves, then on the upper side and other parts; badly infected leaves die but stay on the plant.

ref.where: Tebuconazole 25.9 % m/m EC: groundnut, tikka and rust

seed_rainfed.what: seed for a rainfed direct-sown crop

organic.note: Or plough in 6.25 t/ha of green manure.
Mixed with 50 kg FYM and 25 kg sand, broadcast before transplanting.

protect.name: Yellow stem borer
protect.signs: Larvae bore into the central shoot, which dries ("dead heart"); in grown plants the whole panicle dries and stays white ("white ear"); hit shoots pull out easily.
protect.threshold: 2 egg masses per m2, or 10 % dead hearts, or 2 % white ears

prevent.note: To watch for stem borer and leaf folder moths.

ref.where: Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 % SC: rice, stem borer and leaf folder

protect.name: Brown planthopper
protect.signs: Hoppers crowd at the base of the plants above the water; plants dry up in round patches ("hopper burn"); sooty mould at the base.
protect.threshold: 1 hopper per tiller, or 2 per tiller when spiders are about 1 per hill

prevent.text: Avoid too much nitrogen and close planting; leave a 30 cm lane every 2.5 m.

ref.where: Azadirachtin 0.03 % neem oil based EC: rice, leaf roller, stem borer, BPH
Pymetrozine 50 % WG: paddy, brown plant hopper
Thiamethoxam 30 % FS: sorghum, shoot fly, seed dresser

protect.name: Shoot fly
protect.signs: The maggot bores into the stem and cuts the growing point: the central shoot dries ("dead heart") and the plant puts out side tillers.
protect.threshold: 1 egg per plant in 10 % of plants in the first two weeks, or 10 % dead hearts

prevent.note: Keep them until the crop is 30 days old.

prevent.text: Sow early, soon after the monsoon sets in.

ref.where: Metalaxyl-M 31.8 % ES: pearl millet, downy mildew, seed dresser

protect.name: Downy mildew (green ear)
protect.signs: Leaves yellow from the base upward with white growth underneath; plants stunted and without heads, or heads turned into leafy structures ("green ear").

prevent.text: Pull out and destroy infected plants up to 45 days after sowing.

protect.name: Blast
protect.signs: Spindle-shaped brown spots on the leaves that join up and dry the foliage; the neck of the head turns black and shrinks (neck blast).

organic.text: Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens 0.2 % (2 g per litre).

organic.note: At the last ploughing, against fall armyworm.

ref.where: Thiamethoxam 30 % FS: maize, stem fly, seed dresser

protect.name: Fall armyworm
protect.signs: Young larvae scrape the leaf surface; older larvae eat into the central whorl, the tassel and the cob.

prevent.note: Mass trapping from 10 to 15 days after sowing.

prevent.text: Border crop of cowpea, sunflower or sesame; intercrop black gram or green gram.

organic.text: Early whorl stage, 15 to 20 days after sowing.

conventional.text: Early whorl stage, 15 to 20 days after sowing.

organic.note: With 50 kg of well-rotted FYM or sand, to the soil, against wilt.

protect.name: Pod borer (Helicoverpa)
protect.signs: Larvae thrust their heads into the pods with the rest of the body hanging out; pods with round holes.

ref.where: NPV of Helicoverpa armigera 2.0 % AS: pigeon pea, pod borer

organic.text: While the larvae are young (up to the third instar).

ref.where: Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 % SC: pigeon pea, pod borer

protect.name: Wilt
protect.signs: Leaves go pale and droop; plants wilt from the bottom up and die in patches; dark streaks under the bark at the stem base.

prevent.text: Seed treatment with Trichoderma and soil application of Pseudomonas at 30 days (in the feeding schedule).

organic.note: With 50 kg of well-rotted FYM or sand, against wilt.

protect.name: Gram pod borer (Helicoverpa)
protect.signs: Larvae thrust their heads into the pods with the rest of the body hanging out; pods with round holes.
protect.threshold: 2 young larvae per plant, or 5 to 8 eggs per plant

ref.where: NPV of Helicoverpa armigera 2.0 % AS: gram, pod borer
Emamectin benzoate 5 % SG: chickpea, pod borer

protect.name: Fusarium wilt
protect.signs: Seedlings collapse 3 to 5 weeks after sowing; older plants droop and die, in patches; the inside of the stem turns dark.

prevent.text: Pseudomonas to the soil before sowing (in the feeding schedule).

protect.name: Leafhopper (jassid)
protect.signs: Leaves turn pale yellow, edges go pinkish brown and curl inward under heavy attack.

ref.where: Imidacloprid 17.8 % SL: sunflower, jassid, thrips, whitefly

protect.name: Downy mildew
protect.signs: The first true leaves turn yellow; seedlings damp off or stay stunted.

protect.name: Leafhopper (jassid)
protect.signs: Leaves curl down and turn red, brick red under heavy attack; growth stops.

prevent.text: Intercrop pulses (cowpea, green gram, black gram) to keep sucking pests down.

protect.name: Whitefly
protect.signs: Yellow spots, leaves curl up and turn reddish and brittle; sticky honeydew spoils the lint.

Flonicamid 50 % WG: cotton, aphids, jassids, thrips and whiteflies

protect.name: Pink bollworm
protect.signs: Flowers stay closed like a rosette; buds and young bolls drop; bore holes with excreta; stained lint and eaten seeds.

organic.text: Release the egg parasitoid Trichogrammatoidea bactrae, 40,000 per ha, three times at 15-day intervals from 45 days after sowing.

ref.where: Emamectin benzoate 5 % SG: cotton, boll worms

protect.name: Thrips
protect.signs: Leaves crinkle and curl upward with long stalks; buds turn brittle and drop; early attack stunts the plants.

ref.where: Spinosad 45.0 % SC: chillies, fruit borer, thrips

protect.name: Yellow (muranai) mite
protect.signs: Leaves curl down and crinkle, with long stalks; plants stunted.

protect.name: Fruit rot and die-back
protect.signs: Flowers drop and dry; twigs die back from the tip; branches wither; fruits rot.

organic.text: Three sprays 15 days apart from the first signs.

protect.name: Fruit borer (Helicoverpa)
protect.signs: Young larvae eat tender leaves; grown larvae bore round holes in the fruit, half the body inside.

prevent.text: Grow marigold as a border crop.

protect.name: Whitefly and leaf curl
protect.signs: Yellow spots, yellowing, leaves curl down and dry; it spreads tomato leaf curl virus.

prevent.text: Remove the weed host Abutilon indicum.

organic.text: Spray a neem formulation (1 %) or neem seed kernel extract (5 %).

protect.name: Early blight
protect.signs: Brown spots with rings like a bull's eye and a yellow edge on the leaves; brown rings on the fruit near the stalk.

ref.where: Azoxystrobin 23 % SC: tomato, early and late blight

protect.name: Mango hoppers
protect.signs: Hoppers suck the sap of the flower stalks: flowers wither and drop; honeydew and sooty mould on the leaves; a clicking sound among the leaves.

prevent.text: Remove criss-cross, infested and dense branches.

organic.text: Apply Metarhizium anisopliae or Beauveria bassiana (10^8 cfu/ml) on the trunk.

ref.where: Imidacloprid 17.8 % SL: mango, hopper, 2-4 ml per tree in 10 litres

conventional.text: In 10 litres of water per tree.

protect.name: Powdery mildew
protect.signs: White powder on leaves, flowers, flower stalks and fruits; fruits stop growing and drop before pea size.

protect.name: Fruit fly
protect.signs: Maggots bore into ripening fruits: decayed spots, oozing, brown rotten patches, fruits drop.

prevent.text: Plough between the trees to expose the pupae; collect and destroy fallen fruits.
